newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chateau d'Yquem seller says deal in order - paper.
newsitem.headline: Chateau d'Yquem seller says deal in order - paper.

text.p: Marquis Eugene de Lur Saluces, who has agreed to sell the acclaimed Chateau d'Yquem vineyard to luxury goods group LVMH despite his brother's opposition, says the sale does not require their joint approval, the newspaper Le Monde reported on Wednesday.

Count Alexandre de Lur Saluces, who has managed the property near Bordeaux for 28 years and holds a minority share, said on Monday he would contest the deal struck late last month. He said in a statement that a 1968 agreement "prohibits any sale without the unanimous consent of the two brothers".
Eugene de Lur Saluces was quoted in Le Monde as saying he was "not bound by any joint-ownership agreement".
LVMH announced on November 28 that it had concluded an agreement with several members of the family to acquire around 55 percent of Chateau d'Yquem, which produces sweet golden Sauterne wines.
The company said it had struck an agreement with Eugene de Lur Saluces but that his brother Alexandre refused to sell.
